subject: PO field requirements, itemization standard & issuance timing
messages:

Date: Tue, 02 May 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: PO format and issuance cadence for onboarding

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for agreeing to onboard BrightBridge as a Redwood supplier. We're kicking off vendor setup on our side and want to align on the PO requirements and cadence so we can issue the first PO without delays. Quick list of items we need clarified from you: 

- Mandatory fields Redwood requires on a PO (legal/vendor name, tax id, remit address, cost center/account code, etc.)
- Preferred granularity for line items (single consolidated line vs. itemized per service/feature)
- Any required SKU/code mapping we should include on the PO
- Invoicing preferences (per PO vs. consolidated monthly) and the AP email to send invoices to
- Typical internal timeline from vendor approval -> PO issuance once we provide tax/docs

Attached is our vendor onboarding form (BrightBridge_Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf) and AP terms for your reference. Ideally we want a pilot PO in the next 10 business days; let us know if that aligns with Redwood's process.

If helpful, happy to schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Erin Reynolds
Procurement Lead
BrightBridge Inc.
[Attachment: BrightBridge_Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
To: BrightBridge Procurement <procurement@brightbridge.com>, accounts-payable@brightbridge.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 02 May 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO format and issuance cadence for onboarding

Thanks Erin — welcome, excited to get this moving. High-level answers up front, followed by a short checklist so your AP team has everything to issue a clean PO.

Redwood PO required fields (must appear on the PO or in an accompanying cover sheet):
- Redwood legal name (Redwood Inference, Inc.) and remit address
- Redwood Tax ID / EIN
- PO number (generated by BrightBridge)
- Line-item description, unit price, qty, and extended total
- Unit of measure (e.g., GPU-hour, seat, license-month)
- Billing period or start/end date for services
- Cost center / project code (if applicable)
- Contact for PO inquiries (procurement@redwood.ai)

Preferred line-item structure: we prefer itemization that maps to billing dimensions. For inference services that typically looks like:
- Model Inference - [model name/variant] — unit: GPU-hour — qty — unit price
- Embeddings — unit: 1K tokens — qty — unit price
- Support / Professional Services — unit: day or flat fee

We can accept either:
- One detailed PO with multiple itemized lines (recommended), OR
- A single top-line PO with a required attachment that contains the itemization mapping (less preferred).

Invoice routing / frequency: we support per-PO invoices or consolidated monthly invoices. Please indicate on the PO which you prefer and the AP email to send invoices to; our default accounting inbox is accounting@redwood.ai.

Timeline and cutover: once we receive completed vendor onboarding + tax docs (W-9 equivalent), typical internal routing is:
1) Procurement submission -> Finance validation (1 business day)
2) Finance issues initial pilot PO (3 business days after validation)
3) Pilot activation and 30-day monitoring -> then move to recurring PO cadence if all good

So, target: pilot PO within 5 business days from receipt of completed forms/tax docs.

I've attached our PO template (Redwood_PO_Template.xlsx) and a short example CSV mapping for line-item codes. Questions for you:
- Do you have a preferred unit_of_measure mapping for GPU usage?
- Will BrightBridge accept a PO that references our cost-center as a string (e.g., CC-ML-401) or do you require a numeric account code?

Looping in Neha (Finance) and Dev (Ops) to confirm the recommended itemization and any edge cases (e.g., pre-paid credits, metered minimums).

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Vendor Programs Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_PO_Template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: dev.patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: PO format and issuance cadence for onboarding

Quick notes from an operations perspective — add these to the checklist if helpful.

Suggested line-item taxonomy (keeps billing and usage alignment simple):
- SKU: RI-INFER-<model>-GPUHR — Description: Model inference (on-demand) — UOM: GPU-hour — Rate: $/GPU-hr
- SKU: RI-EMB-1K-TOK — Description: Embeddings — UOM: 1K tokens — Rate: $ per 1K tokens
- SKU: RI-SUPPORT-PSH — Description: Professional services / support hours — UOM: hour or day
- SKU: RI-PREPAY-CRED — Description: Prepaid credit top-up — UOM: USD — Rate: N/A (balance)

Examples to include on the PO:
- If charging for GPU-hours, include an expected billing cadence (daily vs monthly usage) and an estimated baseline for monitoring during the pilot.
- For monthly consolidated invoices, include a reference column on the PO that lists underlying usage PO numbers (if there are multiple POs within the month).

Edge cases:
- If BrightBridge requires a single flat-fee PO for a month, we'll accept it but need an attached usage report to reconcile consumption.
- For pre-paid credits we need a purchase amount and an internal allocation code to tie spend to that PO.

Cutover timeline proposal (ops-approved):
- Day 0: BrightBridge submits vendor onboarding form + tax docs
- Day 1: Redwood Finance validates vendor details (Neha)
- Day 2-3: Finance issues pilot PO (up to 3 business days)
- Day 4-30: Pilot live & monitoring; usage reporting shared weekly
- Day 31: Decide recurring PO cadence and finalize contract amendments if needed

Attached is a small CSV with suggested SKU->line-item mapping (lineitem_mapping_example.csv).

-Neha, can you confirm the finance validation checklist so we have the precise day-1 criteria?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Platform Ops (Billings)
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: lineitem_mapping_example.csv (text/csv)]
